title: Chapter 21: Files and Paths: Saving and Loading Data
video_title: Python Chapter 21: Files and Paths, Saving and Loading Data
summary: The Corner Cafe quiz forgot every score when it closed. Follow Asha as she writes and reads files with pathlib and open(), chooses the right mode, reads line by line, and saves tables as CSV files. Then watch her build a save function with an AI assistant at all six stages. Her tests catch two confident AI mistakes that lose data with no error.

scenes.title: Why this matters
scenes.direction: Memory versus disk, then real uses.

visual.heading: Why this matters
visual.label: The big picture
items: Variables live in memory. Memory is cleared when the program stops.
A **file** is data saved on the disk, with a name. It stays.
Saved games, settings, sales and spreadsheets are all files.

segments.say: Why did the scores vanish? Variables live in the computer's memory, and memory is cleared when the program stops.
A file is data saved on the disk, with a name. It stays there, so the next run can load it.
Saved games, app settings, a shop's sales: they are all files.

scenes.title: The idea: open, read or write, close
scenes.direction: Teach the three steps, the three modes, the order-book analogy and encoding. Quiz on modes. Breather.

visual.heading: Open, read or write, close
visual.label: The idea
body: A program talks to a file in three steps.
visual.pre:
program                        disk
  +---------+   open("scores.csv")  +-------------+
  | memory  | ------ read -------> | name,score  |
  | (lost   | <----- write ------- | Asha,4      |
  |  at end)|       close          | (stays)     |
  +---------+                      +-------------+

segments.say: A program talks to a file in three steps. Open the file. Read from it, or write to it. Then close it.
The memory side is lost at the end. The disk side stays.

visual.heading: The mode says what you want
visual.label: The idea
rows: Reads the file. The default. The file must exist.
Creates the file, or empties it first.
Adds to the end. Creates the file if needed.

segments.say: When you open a file, the mode says what you want to do.
R reads. It is the default, and the file must already exist.
W writes. It creates the file, or empties it first if it already exists.
A appends. It adds to the end, and creates the file if it is missing.

visual.heading: A file is like the cafe's order book
visual.label: Analogy
items: You can read it, start a new book, or add a line at the end.
Unlike a person, mode `"w"` empties the book with no warning.

segments.say: Think of the cafe's order book. You can read it, start a new empty book, or add a line at the end.
But a person would never tear out every page by accident. Mode W empties the file with no warning.

visual.heading: Text and encoding
visual.label: The idea
body: A file stores bytes. An **encoding** turns letters into bytes and back.
UTF-8 stores every language, including the é in Café.
Always write `encoding="utf-8"`, so your program works the same on every computer.

segments.say: One more idea. A file stores bytes, not letters. An encoding is the rule that turns letters into bytes, and back.
UTF-8 is the standard. It stores every language, including the e with an accent in Café. So always write encoding equals utf 8.

visual.question: Asha wants to add a line to the end of a file and keep the old lines. Which mode?
visual.explain: `"a"` appends: it adds to the end and keeps what is there.

segments.say: Quick check. Asha wants to add a line and keep the old ones. Which mode?

after.say: B. Append. W would empty the file first.

items: Memory is lost; files stay.
Open, read or write, close.
`"w"` empties, `"a"` adds, `"r"` reads.

segments.say: Breather. Three steps, three modes. That is the whole idea.
Next, Asha writes her first file.

scenes.title: Steps 6 and 7: CSV files
scenes.direction: Write a CSV file, then read one with DictReader. Teach strings before the ask and the quiz.

visual.heading: Step 6: Write a CSV file

segments.say: Step 6. A CSV file stores a table as text: one row per line, with commas between the values.
Line 4 opens it with newline equals empty. The Python documentation asks for this, so the C S V module controls the line endings.
Line 5 makes a writer. Each writerow takes a list, and writes one row. The first row is the header: the column names.
Asha reads the file back.

scenes.title: Work with AI: a save function that keeps every score
scenes.direction: Safety first. Six stages on save_score. Stage 3 plants mode w; tests catch it; debug a missing folder; improve breaks the header rule.

visual.heading: This chapter's AI skill: safe file handling
visual.label: Before you start
items: Some file mistakes destroy data with no error.
Test file code on a copy, then read the file afterwards.
Customer names and scores are private: paste a made-up sample.

segments.say: This chapter's AI skill is safe file handling. Some file mistakes destroy data with no error at all.
So test file code on a copy, and read the file afterwards.
And never paste private data. A file of real names and scores is private, so paste a made-up sample.

visual.heading: Plan: file, format and mode

messages.text: I am a beginner. My quiz app must save a name and a score after every round, so the next run can load them. Do not write code yet. Which file, format and mode should I use?

1. A CSV file, scores.csv, with the header name,score.
2. Mode "a", so the old rows stay.
3. Write the header only when the file is new.
4. Open it with newline="" and encoding="utf-8".

segments.say: Stage 1: plan. Asha describes the data to save, and asks for no code yet.
The AI suggests a C S V file, mode A, and a header only when the file is new. That matches what you learned.

visual.heading: Write it yourself, then check

messages.text: I wrote this function myself. Do not rewrite it. What happens to the file on the first call, and on the second?

First call: the file is new, so it writes the header, then Asha's row.
Second call: the file exists, so it adds only Omar's row.
I called it twice and read the file. It matches:

segments.say: Stage 2: write. Asha writes her own save function first. Line 7 asks if the file is new. Lines 10 and 11 write the header only then.
She asks the AI to explain what each call does to the file, without rewriting it.
She calls it twice, and reads the file. It matches the explanation.

messages.text: Write save_score(path, name, score). It saves a quiz score to a CSV file with a header. It must keep every score.
Here it is. It keeps every score you save.

segments.say: Look at line 6, and remember the three modes. Lines 11 and 12 save Asha, then Omar.

ask.question: The AI says it keeps every score. Is it right?

after.say: No. Asha's score is gone. Mode W empties the file on every call, so only Omar survives.

visual.heading: Test: the exact file after each case

messages.text: Give me test cases for save_score. For each one, write the exact text the file should hold afterwards.

1. New file, save Asha: the header, then Asha,4.
2. Two saves, Asha then Omar: the header and both rows.
3. An old file with Asha, save Lina: Lina after Asha.

segments.say: Stage 4: test. Asha asks for test cases, each with the exact text the file should hold.
The AI lists three: a new file, two saves, and an old file with data in it.

visual.heading: The three cases, on the AI's function

segments.say: She runs all three cases on the AI's function. Case 1 passes. Cases 2 and 3 fail: both lost a row, with no error.

visual.heading: The fixed function: append, header only when new

segments.say: The AI fixes it: mode A, and the header only when the file is new. The same idea as Asha's own version.
Two saves now keep both rows.

visual.heading: Stage 5: a save into a folder

segments.say: Stage 5: debug. Asha moves the scores into a data folder. Line 15 saves to data, slash, week dot c s v.
File not found! The report points at line 8, inside the function.

visual.heading: Debug: the cause before the fix

messages.text: I moved the scores into a data folder. Line 15 now saves to data/week.csv, and I got FileNotFoundError: No such file or directory: 'data/week.csv'. First explain the cause. Then show the smallest fix.

Line 8 opens data/week.csv, but there is no data folder. Mode "a" creates a missing file, not a missing folder.
Fix: start the function with Path(path).parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True). It makes the folder only if it is missing.

segments.say: She pastes the error into the chat, and asks for the cause first.
The AI explains. Mode A creates a missing file, but not a missing folder. The fix makes the folder, only if it is missing.

visual.heading: Every case again, plus the folder

segments.say: Line 7 is the fix. Then Asha runs every case again, plus a fourth: a file in a folder. All four pass.

visual.heading: Improve: one suggestion, then every test

messages.text: All four cases pass. Suggest at most one improvement, with one reason. Do not change what the file contains.
Remove the exists check and write the header on every save. It is simpler, and CSV readers skip repeated headers.

segments.say: Stage 6: improve. Asha asks for one improvement that does not change the file.
The AI says: write the header on every save, because C S V readers skip repeated headers.

visual.heading: The AI's shorter version, on every case

segments.say: Here is the shorter version. Line 10 writes the header every time. Remember how Dict reader finds its column names.

ask.question: Will case 2, two saves, still pass?

after.say: No. Cases 2 and 3 fail: the header is written twice.
And Dict reader uses only the first row as the header, so the second header becomes a data row. The AI was wrong again. Asha keeps her check.

scenes.title: Common mistakes
scenes.direction: Mistake 1 is a typo in a file name. Mistakes 2 and 4 are spot-it asks. Then a table and a quiz.

visual.heading: Mistake 1: a file name that does not match

segments.say: Mistake 1. The file is called scores, with an s. Line 3 asks for score, without one.
Line 2 printed, then Python stopped: file not found, with the exact name it looked for.
Check the spelling, and run the program from the folder that holds the file. A relative path is looked up in the working directory.

visual.heading: Mistake 2: your turn to spot it
visual.note: log.txt has three lines before this program runs.
visual.hidden_text: Find the problem before the file appears.

segments.say: Now you try. The cafe log has three lines. This program meant to add one more.

ask.question: How many lines does the log have after this program runs?

after.say: One. Mode W emptied the file first. There was no error, and the three old lines are gone.
after.heading: Mistake 2: mode w when you meant a

after.say: The fix: use A to add. Use W only when you want to start again.

visual.heading: Mistake 3: the wrong encoding

segments.say: Mistake 3. An old cash register saved its menu with a different encoding. Reading it as UTF-8 fails at the e with an accent.
Find out which encoding saved the file, read it once with that encoding, and save it again as UTF-8.

visual.heading: Mistake 4: spot it
visual.hidden_text: Find the problem before the error appears.

segments.say: One more. Remember what Dict reader gives back.

after.say: The price is text, and Python cannot add text to a float.
after.heading: Mistake 4: using CSV values as numbers

after.say: The fix: convert first, with float.

visual.heading: Four file mistakes
visual.label: Common mistakes
rows: A wrong name, folder or working directory
Check the name and where you run it
Read it with its encoding, save as UTF-8

segments.say: Here are all four.
File not found: a wrong name, folder or working directory.
No error, but data gone: W instead of A.
Unicode decode error: the file used another encoding.
And a type error with a string: a C S V value is text.

after.say: A. File not found. Python names the file it looked for.

items: Check the file name and the working directory.
Use `"a"` to add.
CSV values are text.

scenes.title: Recap
scenes.direction: Each recap point appears as it is spoken, then the badge.

visual.heading: Recap
visual.label: What you learned
items: A file keeps data after the program stops.
`write_text()` and `read_text()` write and read a whole file.
`with open(...)` closes the file for you. `"w"` empties, `"a"` adds, `"r"` reads.
Always write `encoding="utf-8"`. `strip()` removes each line's newline.
`csv.writer` writes rows. `csv.DictReader` reads them as dictionaries of text.
Test file code on a copy, and read the file afterwards.

segments.say: Let's recap. A file keeps data after the program stops.
Write text and read text work on a whole file.
With open closes the file for you. W empties, A adds, R reads.
Always write encoding equals utf 8, and strip each line.
The C S V module writes rows, and reads them as dictionaries of text.
And test file code on a copy, then read the file.
Mission complete! You earned 100 XP and the Archivist badge.
